title: USMNT Player Ratings vs. Canada: American Boys See Out Perfect Fall Window
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Sophia VeselyOct 6, 2026Justin Ellis (right) had the game winner on Tuesday. / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesThe U.S. men’s national team saw out a perfect fall, winning its fourth-consecutive match on Tuesday night with a 1–0 result against Canada.

The affair at Allianz Field in St. Paul—although not as goal-frenzied as the previous wins against Peru, Chile and Mexico—nonetheless proved the Stars and Stripes’ steady dominance and their incredibly bright future.
It also marked the USMNT’s first win against Canada since 2024 and of manager Mauricio Pochettino’s tenure.

The Argentine boss will be incredibly pleased with how his team prevailed over the past two weeks and the contributions his several newcomers made, including 19-year-old Justin Ellis’s game-winner in the first half.

Justin Ellis (right) had the game winner on Tuesday. /  Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty ImagesIt was a look of relief, rather than excitement, on Ellis’s face upon scoring in the 29th minute, a goal that would prove to be the game-winner.

The young striker was no doubt in agonizing pain in that moment, having suffered a major ankle injury less than 10 minutes prior, thanks to a swift kick to the leg from Canadian midfielder Stephen Eustaquio.

Upon that tackle, Ellis fell immediately to the pitch, curled up, clutching his lower leg. After medical assistance, Ellis was able to stand up by himself, but he had an intense limp. Nevertheless, he refused to leave the pitch. He was on a mission to find the back of the net, no matter how much it hurt.

So when the opportunity arose just seven minutes later, the teenager wasn’t going to waste it. He didn’t know how much more his ankle had left to give. Sprinting (or rather, hobbling) into Canada’s penalty box, he met a pinpointed cross from fullback Alex Freeman. Ellis threw his leg out frantically, redirecting the ball into the back of the net.
Pochettino will not soon forget the grit and determination that Ellis showed throughout the first half, and that play alone may have solidified him another call-up in November.
Alex Freeman was brilliant on Tuesday night. /  David Berding/USSF/Getty Images*Ratings provided by FotMob*
GK: Brian Schwake—7.3: Solid display in his first-career start, but wasn’t incredibly tested.

RB: Alex Freeman—8.4: Shut winger Liam Millar down effectively in the corner with strong one-vs.-one defending. His keen vision regarding when to make dangerous runs into the final third—and the foot skills he often employs to do so—continues to set him apart. Had a brilliant assist for Ellis.
CB: Chris Richards—6.8: Effective in gradually pushing up the backline in possession to put Canada on its back heels.
CB: George Campbell—6.8: Had a big clearance from the penalty box in the 23rd minute after a moment of carelessness from partner Richards. Almost had an own goal in the 67th minute.

LB: Auston Trusty—6.7: Performed better at center back than left back this fall. Nonetheless, his ability to do both could make him indispensable for Pochettino moving forward. Trusty is also confident taking control of the air on defensive set-pieces.

CM: Brooklyn Raines—6.9: Looked much more at ease in the midfield than he did against Chile and carved out a discernible role for himself as distributor and ball-winner. He also pulled some silky moves, much to the Canada defenders’ dismay.
CM: Yunus Musah—6.1: Had a few bursts of dynamic movement, but mostly looked slow and stiff.

RW: Giovanni Reyna—6.9: Only player to start all four matches this window. Quickly establishing himself as Pochettino’s right-hand man. Could be a consistent starter in Concacaf Nations League play next month.

AM: Malik Tillman—7.2: He was everywhere throughout the central zone of the field. His ability to get involved in every facet of the midfield as well as on the front line makes him the creative heartbeat of the attack.
